scenarios.name: secure-compose-persistent-deploy
scenarios.rationale: A covers every rubric item (both volumes, loopback bind, API key, THREADS=4, pinned tag, though it admits it hasn't confirmed the tag exists), while B uses `latest` and only says to pin it later, which is weaker than an explicit recommendation, though it does persist both volumes, bind to loopback, set the key and threads.

scenarios.name: custom-gguf-model-yaml
scenarios.rationale: Both responses meet every rubric item: name: mistral, backend: llama-cpp, top-level context_size, threads and gpu_layers: 0, the GGUF filename under parameters.model, baseURL http://localhost:8080/v1, and model 'mistral'; B states outright that these keys are top-level and not under parameters and explains that the client model must match the YAML name, while A adds extras such as f16, mmap and a template block and its note about the system role is questionable.

scenarios.name: offline-embeddings-for-openai-client
scenarios.rationale: B matches the rubric closely: it uses the sentencetransformers backend with all-MiniLM-L6-v2, mentions the llama-cpp option, tells the user to restart the container, and verifies with a curl that returns 384. A has the right model YAML, embeddings: true and a 384-length curl check, but it never says the container needs a restart or reload to pick up the new YAML.
